notes:
Account snapshot: Aurum Bridge runs an enterprise contact center platform used by retail & travel verticals. Primary goal: reduce live-agent contacts via ticket deflection and strong first-contact answer rates. They operate a knowledge base ~200M documents (mix of FAQs, transcripts, KB articles). Current infra: in-house vector store (Qdrant) + Elasticsearch for metadata. Pain: p99 latency spikes during peak hours -> SLA misses for response within 150ms. Cost pressure: want OPEX comparable to current vector infra (< $0.01/query for typical rerank flow).

Technical requirements (from SE call):
- Indexing scale: support 150M-250M vectors, incremental updates at ~500k docs/day.
- Embedding model: prefer 1536-d embeddings (open model) but open to Redwood-provided optimized variants.
- Query profile: 80% single-query QPS spikes to 1000 qps peak, baseline 200 qps.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 80ms, p99 <= 180ms for full RAG (embedding search + top-5 rerank).
- Reranking goal: top-5 precision/quality metric target >= 92% in our internal evals.
- Cost target: average end-to-end cost per user query < $0.005 (embeddings + rerank compute amortized).
- Security: SSO (SAML), strict audit logs, customer-managed KMS, logs retention 7 years, EU-data residency for subset of clients.

Notes from demo: good reaction to Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching + quantization profiles). They liked Dedicated for predictable throughput but want Private control plane for tenancy isolation. Asked pointed questions about fallback model variants during capacity constraints and how routing prioritizes latency SLAs vs cost. SE recommended a hybrid: Dedicated GPU pools with private control plane and a fallback hosted variant for cost bursts.

Stated quote from Head of Product: "We need deterministic 99th percentile — if we miss p99 during holiday peak we lose customers."

Next steps (short): send POC SOW, include 3-week test ingest (50M vectors) + target telemetry (p95/p99/resolution rate), provide KMS + SAML wiring doc, a sample cost model with Dedicated vs Private.
